checkpoints.description: [2/3] Milestone: three twin triples + registry entries + TwinParityTest (8 cases green) + RegistryShapeTest
[3/3] Verification: 335 tests pass; formal 8-case harness run recorded; README table + standings + ADR-026; knowledge base synced
[1/4] Plan: close call_chain (attributed binds, then small-function inlining), binary_gcd (constant division by reciprocal multiply), nqueens last (spill/frame work); measure, ADR, commit

impact_assessment.why: user ordered 'get faster': three committed cases sit behind at least one baseline, worst call_chain 2.7x C — the scoreboard commitment is at or ahead on every case
impact_assessment.benefits: contract: no semantics change anywhere the shape gates refuse; the strict goal becomes green when all closures measure
impact_assessment.risks: contract: argument reordering on bind (impure operands still evaluate once, left to right); dependency: inlining reuses the pair-copy engine and must not fire on loops/calls in bodies; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: every new pass is a silent fallback on refusal; ParityTest + full suite (335) plus e2e probes gate each milestone; measure before and after; revert any variant that measures worse (the delta-nonzero precedent)

checkpoints.description: [3/4] Land M2 backend batch + magic division: foreign-function inlining (call-free/loop-free/label-free callee copies under fn.<name>.copy.N), branchless select (sub+lea+cmovcc), direct-into-register compute with strict rax-shape gate, two-homed compare, magic-multiply division for positive literal / and % (search proves int64 exactness at two inequality worst points + INT64_MIN; reproduces gcc's 2147483647 params; no DIV_ZERO trap remains at magic sites). Measurements: call_chain 95.9->45-48 ms (Rust beaten 0.62x, C 1.3x pending); binary_gcd 190.2->178-195 ms (C 1.08x, Rust 1.28x). 363 tests + 39 subtests pass incl. byte-parity twin gate. ADR-027 recorded; README rows + prose updated; codebase map refreshed. checklists: passed

[4/4] Commit 32f8ac3 landed (9 files, 1235 insertions): m2 backend batch + magic division with ADR-027, README standings, refreshed codebase map and ledger. Suite 363 + 39 subtests; project gates 4/4 passed earlier in the phase and re-verified by check before commit. Remaining recorded targets: call_chain vs C (1.3x), binary_gcd vs C/Rust via flag-fused bit conditions (bgcd setcc lowering) and nqueens spill/frame work (deferred by design). checklists: passed
Phase 4 re-verified after commit 32f8ac3: aikit.py check cairn --strict gates 4/4 PASS (test 24.0s, hygiene, guidelines freshness, secrets)

[1/2] Plan: benchmark-regression watch -- run_benchmarks.py gains --save (append one JSONL record per run to .aikit/benchmark_history.jsonl with commit stamp) so --compare diffs the newest saved record per-case and exits nonzero on a Cairn regression beyond the documented 10% noise band; pure compare_runs() carries the logic; failing-first tests; README + project guideline record the rule: benchmarks re-run after every compiler change

impact_assessment.why: user's standing 'get faster' plus ADR-026 targets means a compiler change can win one case while silently losing another; only a same-run comparison catches it
impact_assessment.benefits: regressions surface at the change that caused them, with commit stamps in history; the strict scoreboard gets an automatic pre-flight
impact_assessment.risks: contract: compare reads its own saved JSONL only, no semantics change to reports; dependency: git rev-parse may be absent (commit stamped None, compare still works); concurrency: appends are single-agent; state: history file lives in .aikit next to the ledger and is tracked
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first tests for compare_runs (regressed/improved/new/within-noise); corrupted history lines skipped; first-ever --compare with empty history prints guidance and exits 0

checkpoints.description: [2/2] Regression watch landed: run_benchmarks.py --save appends commit-stamped JSONL records to .aikit/benchmark_history.jsonl, --compare diffs per case at the 10% noise band and exits 1 on regression (Cairn column only). CompareRunsTest (8, failing-first) green; live save/compare loop exercised at 32f8ac3 with exit 0. Guideline G-004 records the rule (user source); ADR-028 + README updated; knowledge map refreshed. aikit.py check cairn: 4/4 gates. checklists: passed

[1/3] Plan: flag-fused conditions -- route (x & literal) == 0 / != 0 and x == 0 / x != 0 and small-literal comparison branches straight from test/cmp flags to jcc, deleting the setcc/movzx/test round-trip (7 instr -> 2-4); plus eliding branch-to-next instructions that _emit_if emits when the condition target label sits at the current address. Targets: binary_gcd shift loops, nqueens bit scans, xorshift parity; measured with the ADR-028 --save --compare watch

impact_assessment.why: ADR-027 recorded the exact mechanism (bgcd pays setcc/movzx/test/branch where gcc tests flags) and binary_gcd/nqueens remain behind C and Rust
impact_assessment.benefits: fewer instructions and a shorter dependency chain in every hot bit-test loop; all three open scoreboard pairings benefit
impact_assessment.risks: contract: pure branch lowering, no semantics change if the flag routing is exact (== 0 -> jz, != 0 -> jnz); dependency: test_imm maxes at 127 so literals above it need the reg path; concurrency: none; state: none
impact_assessment.mitigation: failing-first branch-shape tests; full suite + twin-parity; ADR-028 --save --compare before commit, revert if worse

checkpoints.description: flag-fused conditions landed: generalized bit-test branches (x % 2**b, x & m) and short-circuit &&/|| lowering in _emit_condition/_emit_comparison_branch; 400 tests + 39 subtests green; benchmarks --save --compare exit 0 (binary_gcd -7pct, ackermann -14pct, no regression); ADR-029 + README updated; knowledge base verified
Phase 4 verified: suite 400+39 green at a538dcd, cairn strict gate 4/4, compare exit 0; committed perf(codegen) fuse bit-test and logical conditions
Phase 4 checklist outcome: suite 400+39 green at a538dcd, aikit check cairn --strict 4/4 passed, secrets and README gates passed, benchmark compare exit 0

impact_assessment.why: The scoreboard rests on eight cases; whole bottleneck classes (multiply-latency chains, three-argument recursion, division-heavy nested loops, fixed-point inner escapes) are unmeasured, so the next optimizations risk overfitting to measured paths.
impact_assessment.benefits: Four new triple-twin benchmarks extend coverage to tak, primes, mandelbrot and splitmix, and each new case is permanently gated by the twin-parity and regression-watch machinery.
impact_assessment.risks: contract: CASES tuple and TwinParityTest gain entries only, no pipeline contract changes; dependency: only the already-discovered gcc and rustc toolchains; concurrency: none, the harness is sequential; state: .aikit/benchmark_history.jsonl gains new-case records only and --compare claims nothing about cases seen for the first time. Language-semantics drift (signed overflow in C, arithmetic shift) is contained by uint64_t accumulators in the C twin where wrapping is load-bearing.
impact_assessment.mitigation: Twin-parity tests hard-fail on stdout divergence between the three languages; each triple is compiled and executed manually before entering CASES; loads are tuned to tens of milliseconds before baselines are saved.

checkpoints.description: [2/3-and-3/3 scope] Four twins written and parity-verified; operand-park miscompilation found by splitmix and fixed failing-first (GENERIC_EVAL_REGISTERS guard in _emit_binary_into); suite 425+39 green; baselines saved and compared exit 0; ADR-030 + README + KB done
Phase 4 checklist outcome: suite 425+39 green at d4cc6c6, aikit check cairn --strict 4/4 passed, twin parity for all 12 cases passed, benchmark --save --compare exit 0
